A.explanation: This is $Wv$ for the load alone, $1000 \times 9.81 \times 0.50 \approx 4.9 \text{ kW}$, and omits the extra $1000 \text{ N}$ needed for the hook.

B.explanation: Total force $1000 + 1000 \times 9.81$ multiplied by $0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives about $5400 \text{ W}$.

C.explanation: This is about $mg/v$ for the load alone, $9810/0.50 \approx 20 \text{ kW}$, which wrongly divides by velocity instead of using $P = Fv$.

D.explanation: This is about $F_{total}/v$, $10810/0.50 \approx 22 \text{ kW}$, which wrongly divides the total force by velocity instead of multiplying.

hints: Notice the phrase at a constant velocity - the crane must pull up with $1000 \text{ N}$ for the hook plus the full weight $mg$ of the $1000 \text{ kg}$ load.
Recall for a force parallel to velocity that power is $P = Fv$, so you need the total force in $\text{N}$ times $0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, not divided by velocity.
First calculate the load weight $1000 \times 9.81$, add the $1000 \text{ N}$ hook force, then multiply by $0.50$ and convert $\text{W}$ to $\text{kW}$.
walkthrough: Constant velocity means resultant force is zero, so the crane force must balance all downward resistance. For hook plus load this is $F = 1000 + mg$.
Calculate the load weight: $W = mg = 1000 \times 9.81 = 9810 \text{ N}$.
Add the hook force: $F_{total} = 1000 + 9810 = 10810 \text{ N}$ upward.
Use power for motion with force parallel to velocity: $P = F_{total}v$.
